sources.scope: KJV cross-references and editorial notes for The Modern Day Bible.
sources.text:
Samson and the 300 foxes (Judges 15:4–5, KJV)
Judges says Samson caught 300 foxes, paired them tail to tail, placed a firebrand between each pair, lit the brands, and sent the animals into the Philistines’ fields. The passage reports what burned in the fields. It leaves the fate of the foxes untold.

David, Bathsheba, Uriah, and Nathan’s lamb (2 Samuel 11:2–17; 12:1–9, KJV)
David saw Bathsheba washing, sent for her, and later ordered Uriah placed where he would be killed. Nathan told David about a rich man who took a poor man’s only ewe lamb. David condemned the man because he had no pity. Nathan answered, “Thou art the man,” and held David to his own judgment.

Care for animals and care for the wounded (Proverbs 12:10, Luke 10:30–37, KJV)
Proverbs describes a righteous man caring for his beast. In Luke, a priest and a Levite see the wounded man and pass by. The Samaritan binds his wounds, carries him on his own beast, and pays for his care. Tabor reads the two passages together through the care owed to living beings.

Humans and beasts (Ecclesiastes 3:19, KJV)
Humans are mammals. Ecclesiastes describes humans and beasts as sharing breath and mortality. This is the biblical parallel to Tabor’s biological connection.

How the same standard applies (Hebrews 11:32–34, James 1:8, James 4:7–8, KJV)
Hebrews names Samson and David among its examples of faith. James describes the instability of the double minded and pairs resisting the devil with a call to purify their hearts. Tabor’s theological reading places the praise alongside the acts recorded in Judges and Samuel. Across religious, spiritual, non-spiritual, and non-religious editions, the same question applies. Would you judge the act the same way if someone you didn’t admire had done it?

**Read the deal from the children’s side.** Girls reported sexual abuse. Federal prosecutors drafted an indictment, then agreed behind closed doors to drop the federal case in South Florida. They made that decision without consulting the victims and kept them in the dark after signing. The agreement also promised that the South Florida office would forgo federal prosecution of four named people and any potential co-conspirators. That was a betrayal of the children who came forward. [DOJ review](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/11/12/epstein._executive_summary.pdf) · [District court opinion](https://www.law.cornell.edu/sites/default/files/women-and-justice/Epstein-CASE-NO-08-80736-CIV-MARRA.pdf) · [Eleventh Circuit, In re Wild](https://media.ca11.uscourts.gov/opinions/pub/files/201913843.enb.pdf)

- **Who made the deal?** The federal agreement was signed on **September 24, 2007**, during George W. Bush’s presidency. Bush nominated Alexander Acosta to be U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida. The DOJ review identifies **Acosta as the official who approved the agreement**. The records I reviewed establish Bush’s role in the nomination and Acosta’s role in the deal. [DOJ review](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/11/12/epstein._executive_summary.pdf) · [Bush White House nomination archive](https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/nominations/4.html)
- **What was secret?** Epstein’s **June 30, 2008** Florida guilty plea was public. The federal agreement behind it was filed under seal. Epstein was sentenced to **18 months**, served **less than 13**, and was allowed out for work release for up to **12 hours a day**. The *Palm Beach Post* reported the agreement’s terms after it was unsealed in **2009**. Julie K. Brown’s *Miami Herald* investigation brought it to national attention in **2018**. [DOJ review](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/11/12/epstein._executive_summary.pdf) · [Palm Beach Post clipping in court exhibit](https://media-cdn.rollcall.com/epstein-files/doe-v-us-908-cv-80736-sdfl-2008-247-02.pdf) · [Miami Herald series](https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/article238237729.html)
- **What did the courts decide?** In **2019**, Judge Kenneth Marra found that prosecutors violated victims’ rights under the Crime Victims’ Rights Act. In **2021**, the Eleventh Circuit held that the law gave Courtney Wild no right to enforce those rights through a stand-alone lawsuit without an existing federal criminal proceeding. The appeals court also said prosecutors should have consulted her and the other victims. [District court opinion](https://www.law.cornell.edu/sites/default/files/women-and-justice/Epstein-CASE-NO-08-80736-CIV-MARRA.pdf) · [Eleventh Circuit, In re Wild](https://media.ca11.uscourts.gov/opinions/pub/files/201913843.enb.pdf)

**More than 1,000 victims.** That’s what the DOJ and FBI said their broader review confirmed in July 2025. “Dozens” described the scope alleged in the **2019 New York indictment**, which covered conduct from **2002 through 2005**. The broader memo gives no age breakdown or exact total. The public record supports **more than 1,000** and leaves the full number unknown. [DOJ/FBI memo](https://www.justice.gov/opa/media/1407001/dl) · [2019 federal indictment announcement](https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/jeffrey-epstein-charged-manhattan-federal-court-sex-trafficking-minors)

**Timeline Before the 2008 Plea Deal**

- **August 1996 — Initial FBI Report:** Artist Maria Farmer reported Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to the FBI for sexual assault and child pornography. The FBI did not open an investigation at that time.[[1](https://www.justsecurity.org/119137/timeline-jeffrey-epstein-ghislaine-maxwell/)]
- **March 2005 — Palm Beach Police Investigation:** The Palm Beach Police Department opened a criminal investigation after the stepmother of a 14-year-old girl reported that Epstein had paid her stepdaughter for a massage and sexually abused her. Police identified dozens of underage girls with matching accounts. [[1](https://oversightdemocrats.house.gov/imo/media/doc/the_price_of_non-prosecution.pdf)]
- **May 2006 — State Grand Jury Indictment & FBI Involvement:** Palm Beach Police Chief Michael Reiter pushed for severe charges, but the Palm Beach County State Attorney's Office took the case to a state grand jury, which indicted Epstein on a single count of felony solicitation of prostitution. Dissatisfied with the leniency of the state charge, Chief Reiter referred the case to the FBI, which opened a federal investigation codenamed "Operation Leap Year". [[1](https://www.npr.org/2020/11/12/934265386/jeffrey-epsteins-former-prosecutors-used-poor-judgment-in-deal-doj-says), [2](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/explosive-report-drags-another-president-075723262.html), [3](https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Epstein-Files-A-Timeline), [4](https://www.justsecurity.org/119137/timeline-jeffrey-epstein-ghislaine-maxwell/)]
- **May 2007 — Draft Federal Indictment:** Assistant U.S. Attorney Marie Villafaña in the Southern District of Florida drafted a 53-page, 60-count federal indictment against Epstein, charging him with sex trafficking of minors and enticement of minors to engage in illegal sexual activity. [[1](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/12/17/jeffrey-epstein-files-records-timeline/87716818007/), [2](https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Epstein-Files-A-Timeline)]
- **Summer 2007 — Defense Lobbying & Secret Negotiations:** Epstein assembled a high-powered defense team including Kenneth Starr, Jay Lefkowitz (both of whom had worked alongside U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta at the law firm Kirkland & Ellis and served in Republican administrations), and Alan Dershowitz. Defense attorneys bypassed line prosecutors to negotiate directly with Acosta and petitioned senior officials at the Bush Justice Department in Washington to shut down the federal prosecution. [[1](https://abcnews.com/US/key-takeaways-justice-department-review-jeffrey-epstein-sweetheart/story?id=74222922), [2](https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Epstein-Files-A-Timeline)]
- **September 24, 2007 — Signing of the Non-Prosecution Agreement:** Acosta and Epstein’s attorneys signed the secret NPA, halting the federal indictment. Following the signing, Epstein’s lawyers continued lobbying senior DOJ officials in Washington—including the Criminal Division and the Office of the Deputy Attorney General—for nearly nine months to try to reduce the terms even further before entering a plea. [[1](https://www.wral.com/archive/22120008/), [2](https://abcnews.com/US/key-takeaways-justice-department-review-jeffrey-epstein-sweetheart/story?id=74222922), [3](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/12/17/jeffrey-epstein-files-records-timeline/87716818007/)]

**Specific Terms of the 2007–2008 Deal**

- **No Federal Prosecution:** The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida agreed to drop its federal investigation and file no federal sex-trafficking charges against Epstein.
- **Blanket Immunity for Co-Conspirators:** The agreement granted federal immunity from prosecution to four named female assistants (Sarah Kellen, Adriana Ross, Lesley Groff, and Nadia Marcinkova) as well as "any potential co-conspirators" who may have recruited or abused minors.
- **State-Level Guilty Plea:** On June 30, 2008, Epstein pleaded guilty in Florida state court to two state charges: one count of felony solicitation of prostitution and one count of procuring a minor for prostitution.
- **Sentence and Work Release:** Epstein was sentenced to 18 months in the Palm Beach County stockade followed by 12 months of house arrest. He served just under 13 months. Under a work-release arrangement, he was permitted to leave the jail for up to 12 hours a day, six days a week, to work at his private office in West Palm Beach, where he continued meeting with young women.
- **Sex Offender Registration & Civil Restitution:** Epstein was required to register as a sex offender and agreed not to contest liability in civil lawsuits filed by a specific list of victims identified by federal prosecutors, provided those victims sought damages only under a specific federal statute.
- **Mandatory Secrecy Clause:** At the demand of Epstein's defense team, federal prosecutors included a confidentiality clause keeping the NPA sealed from the public and concealed from the victims. Prosecutors sent letters to victims stating the case was "still under investigation" even after the deal was signed. [[1](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jeffrey-epstein-plea-deal-jail-term-doj-files/), [2](https://www.justice.gov/opr/page/file/1336471/dl), [3](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/a-timeline-of-the-jeffrey-epstein-investigation-and-the-fight-to-make-the-governments-files-public), [4](https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/05/epstein-plea-agreement-obama-fact-check-markwayne-mullin/85528703007/), [5](https://www.wral.com/archive/22120008/), [6](https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Epstein-Files-A-Timeline), [7](https://oversightdemocrats.house.gov/imo/media/doc/the_price_of_non-prosecution.pdf), [8](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/12/17/jeffrey-epstein-files-records-timeline/87716818007/)]

**Key Officials During the Bush Administration**

- **President:** George W. Bush
- **U.S. Attorneys General:** Alberto Gonzales (served until September 2007, when the NPA was signed) and Michael Mukasey (served from November 2007 through the June 2008 guilty plea).
- **U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida:** Alexander Acosta (appointed by George W. Bush; directly approved and signed the NPA).
- **Additional Developments in Released Files:** Reporting on the 2025–2026 document releases and congressional testimony has highlighted ongoing scrutiny into the communications between Epstein's defense team and senior Bush DOJ officials in Washington during the 2007–2008 review process, as well as Acosta's later statement during his 2017 Trump transition vetting that he had been told Epstein "belonged to intelligence". Meanwhile, a coalition of 17 state attorneys general and members of Congress continue to push for the **Epstein Files Transparency Act II** to compel the release of additional internal DOJ communications and unredacted records that remain withheld. [[1](https://www.lawcommentary.com/articles/17-attorneys-general-sue-doj-epstein-files), [2](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/explosive-report-drags-another-president-075723262.html), [3](https://www.wral.com/archive/22120008/), [4](https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/05/epstein-plea-agreement-obama-fact-check-markwayne-mullin/85528703007/)]

- **Summer 2007 — Defense Lobbying & Secret Negotiations:** Epstein assembled a high-powered defense team including Kenneth Starr, Jay Lefkowitz (both of whom had worked alongside U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta at the law firm Kirkland & Ellis and served in Republican administrations), and Alan Dershowitz. - **No Federal Prosecution:** The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida agreed to drop its federal investigation and file no federal sex-trafficking charges against Epstein.
- **Blanket Immunity for Co-Conspirators:** The agreement granted federal immunity from prosecution to four named female assistants (Sarah Kellen, Adriana Ross, Lesley Groff, and Nadia Marcinkova) as well as "any potential co-conspirators" who may have recruited or abused minors.
- **State-Level Guilty Plea:** On June 30, 2008, Epstein pleaded guilty in Florida state court to two state charges: one count of felony solicitation of prostitution and one count of procuring a minor for prostitution.
- **Sentence and Work Release:** Epstein was sentenced to 18 months in the Palm Beach County stockade followed by 12 months of house arrest. He served just under 13 months. Under a work-release arrangement, he was permitted to leave the jail for up to 12 hours a day, six days a week, to work at his private office in West Palm Beach, where he continued meeting with young women.
- **Sex Offender Registration & Civil Restitution:** Epstein was required to register as a sex offender and agreed not to contest liability in civil lawsuits filed by a specific list of victims identified by federal prosecutors, provided those victims sought damages only under a specific federal statute.
- **Mandatory Secrecy Clause:** At the demand of Epstein's defense team, federal prosecutors included a confidentiality clause keeping the NPA sealed from the public and concealed from the victims. - **U.S. Attorneys General:** Alberto Gonzales (served until September 2007, when the NPA was signed) and Michael Mukasey (served from November 2007 through the June 2008 guilty plea).
- **U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida:** Alexander Acosta (appointed by George W. Bush; directly approved and signed the NPA).

**Documented Connections in the Reagan-Era Arena**

While Reagan and Meese did not mention Epstein, historical records, investigative reporting, and the 2025–2026 [**Epstein files**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_files) releases document several intersections between Epstein and key figures, scandals, and attorneys from the Reagan-Meese arena: [[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adnan_Khashoggi), [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_files)]

- **Adnan Khashoggi and the Iran-Contra Scandal.** During the mid-to-late 1980s, Saudi arms dealer [Adnan Khashoggi](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F03lx88\&q=Adnan+Khashoggi) was a financial client of Epstein's consulting firm, Intercontinental Assets Group. At the exact same time, Khashoggi was serving as the central middleman in the Reagan administration’s [**Iran-Contra affair**](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F03tlf\&q=Iran-Contra+affair), facilitating secret U.S.-Israeli arms transfers to Iran financed through the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI). Attorney General Ed Meese oversaw the initial internal Justice Department inquiry into Iran-Contra in November 1986. [[1](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602033927), [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adnan_Khashoggi), [3](https://morningstaronline.co.uk/article/epstein-files-scandal-still-shrouded-secrets), [4](https://www.nytimes.com/1987/08/28/world/aide-says-north-was-to-take-blame.html), [5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cvy1DQt_ZRQ)]
- **Reagan Administration Officials on Epstein's Defense Team.** Two prominent attorneys from the Reagan-Meese Justice Department later represented Epstein in negotiating his secret 2007–2008 non-prosecution agreement:
  - **[Kenneth Starr](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F0grkx\&q=Kenneth+Starr):** Served as Counselor to Attorney General William French Smith (1981–1983) and was appointed by President Reagan to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit in 1983 before serving as Solicitor General. He was a lead architect of Epstein’s 2007 deal.
  - **[Jay Lefkowitz](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F02639rd\&q=Jay+Lefkowitz):** Worked in Reagan-Bush legal circles and later served in the Bush White House; he co-negotiated the 2007 plea deal with U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta.
- **George H.W. Bush (Reagan's Vice President).** While George H.W. Bush did not mention Epstein publicly, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) releases from the [**George H.W. Bush Presidential Library**](https://www.bush41library.gov/digital-research-room/finding-aid/foia/records-jeffrey-epstein-ghislaine-maxwell-etc)contain 1980s and 1990s administrative correspondence involving academic institutions and organizations later connected to Epstein. Additionally, the February 2026 DOJ document release included an unverified raw intake tip mentioning George H.W. Bush, which FBI records noted lacked corroborating evidence.
- **Towers Financial & Reagan-Era Justice Department.** From 1987 to 1989, Epstein worked with [Steven Hoffenberg](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F05pc2qp\&q=Steven+Hoffenberg) at Towers Financial, a Manhattan firm that later collapsed as a $460 million Ponzi scheme. Hoffenberg claimed in subsequent court filings and interviews that Epstein avoided federal prosecution during the late 1980s because he had "traction" inside the Justice Department.
- **Reagan-Appointed Judges in Modern Epstein Cases.** In ongoing litigation over the [**Epstein Files Transparency Act**](https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Epstein-Files-A-Timeline), U.S. District Judge Emmet Sullivan—originally appointed to the bench by Ronald Reagan—presided over court orders compelling the Department of Justice to produce withheld Epstein records. [[1](https://tce.exchange/content/01a0b110-0c98-7176-b9d3-a421beeaab0b)]

**AI can make mistakes, so double-check responses **

Jeffrey Epstein’s rise in the 1980s shows a well-documented social and business intersection with Donald Trump starting in the mid-to-late 1980s. Meanwhile, Edwin Meese III (U.S. Attorney General from 1985 to 1988) operated in overlapping political and defense-contractor circles rather than having a direct, documented relationship with Epstein. 1. Jeffrey Epstein’s 1980s Rise • Exit from Bear Stearns (1981). After teaching math at Manhattan’s Dalton School without a college degree, Epstein joined Bear Stearns in 1976. He rose to limited partner before resigning in 1981 following an internal investigation and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) scrutiny over expense-account abuses and leaked IPO shares. • Intercontinental Assets Group (1982). Epstein launched his own firm, Intercontinental Assets Group (IAG), styling himself as an international "financial bounty hunter" who recovered hidden or stolen money for ultra-wealthy clients and governments. • International Arms & Intelligence Circles (1982–1986). During the early-to-mid 1980s, Epstein worked closely with British defense contractor Sir Douglas Leese—a key architect of the massive UK–Saudi Al-Yamamah arms deal—and connected with Saudi arms dealer Adnan Khashoggi. Associates from this period later stated that Epstein traveled on an Austrian passport under an alias and claimed to work with intelligence agencies. • Towers Financial Corporation (1987). Introduced by Douglas Leese, Epstein joined Steven Hoffenberg at Towers Financial in Manhattan, earning $25,000 a month as a consultant. Towers Financial collapsed in 1993 as a $460 million Ponzi scheme. Hoffenberg served 18 years in prison and testified that Epstein was the uncharged co-architect of the fraud. 2. Where Epstein Intersected with Donald Trump (Mid-to-Late 1980s) • New York & Palm Beach Proximity (1985–1987). Epstein and Trump first crossed paths around 1985 to 1987, shortly after Trump purchased the Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, where Epstein also maintained a residence. In a 2002 New York magazine profile, Trump stated that he had known Epstein for 15 years, calling him a "terrific guy." • Shared Social Circle & Casinos (Late 1980s). Throughout the late 1980s, the two men frequently socialized in Manhattan, Palm Beach, and Atlantic City. According to former Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino executive Jack O'Donnell, Epstein visited Trump's Atlantic City casinos with Trump in 1989 accompanied by young women. • 1980s Allegations in Released DOJ Files. In March 2026, as part of disclosures under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, the Department of Justice released 2019 FBI interview summaries with a woman who alleged that Epstein introduced her to Trump in the 1980s when she was a minor and that both men assaulted her. Trump has denied all allegations of wrongdoing and called the claims unfounded. 3. Where the Timeline Intersects with Attorney General Ed Meese (1981–1988) Edwin Meese III served as Counselor to President Ronald Reagan (1981–1985) and as U.S. Attorney General (1985–1988). Public records and released DOJ files show no direct meetings or personal relationship between Ed Meese and Jeffrey Epstein, though their orbits overlapped in three notable ways during the 1980s: • The DOJ's Non-Prosecution of Towers Financial. During the late 1980s, while Meese led the Justice Department and Rudy Giuliani led the Southern District of New York, Epstein worked alongside Steven Hoffenberg at Towers Financial. Hoffenberg later claimed in court filings and interviews that Epstein escaped federal prosecution in the Towers Financial Ponzi scheme because Epstein "had traction" with the Department of Justice. • Overlapping Defense & Arms Networks (The PROMIS / Iran-Contra Era). Investigative journalists and civil lawsuits (including a 2023 JPMorgan Chase complaint) have pointed out that Epstein’s 1980s mentors—specifically arms dealers Douglas Leese and Adnan Khashoggi—operated in the same international defense and intelligence ecosystems scrutinized during the Reagan-Meese era. Khashoggi was a central middleman in the Iran-Contra affair, which occurred while Meese was Attorney General, and Meese faced separate independent counsel scrutiny over his involvement in a proposed Iraqi oil pipeline deal involving Israeli officials and defense figures. • Indirect Legal & Institutional Links. Later in the 2000s, attorneys who had worked in or alongside the Reagan-Meese Justice Department—most notably Kenneth Starr (who served as Counselor to Attorney General Meese from 1981 to 1983)—became key members of Epstein’s defense team that negotiated his 2007–2008 non-prosecution agreement.

In fact, according to [**Department of Justice records**](https://www.justice.gov/osg/bio/kenneth-w-starr), Starr served as Counselor and Chief of Staff to Reagan's first Attorney General, **William French Smith**, from 1981 to 1983, before Edwin Meese became Attorney General in 1985. [[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Starr), [2](https://firstliberty.org/news/kenneth-w-starr-passes-away-at-76/)]

sources.text:
**The strongest documented link from the Reagan era to Epstein’s 2007 deal is Kenneth Starr.** The Iran-Contra lead runs through Adnan Khashoggi. His role in the arms sales is documented, but the sources I reviewed give no dated record tying Epstein’s work for Khashoggi to a specific arms transaction. I found no direct Reagan–Epstein or Meese–Epstein relationship in those records. [Starr’s congressional biography](https://www.congress.gov/105/chrg/CHRG-105hhrg53367/CHRG-105hhrg53367.pdf) · [DOJ OPR report](https://www.epstein-search.com/document/263/pdf) · [Senate BCCI report](https://irp.fas.org/congress/1992_rpt/bcci/11intel.htm) · [Vicky Ward’s reporting as quoted by Law & Crime](https://lawandcrime.com/high-profile/investigative-journalist-explains-why-jeffrey-epstein-might-have-needed-a-fake-passport/) · [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602033927)

| Connection | What the evidence establishes |
|---|---|
| **Khashoggi → Iran-Contra → Ed Meese** | A Senate investigation documented that Khashoggi financed some of the 1985–1986 arms transactions through BCCI. Independent Counsel Lawrence Walsh documented Meese’s November 1986 inquiry and concluded that Meese was building a case for Reagan’s deniability. On the Epstein side, journalist Vicky Ward cited a source who said Epstein recovered money for Khashoggi. A court record independently places Epstein at I.A.G. in **1984**, in a transaction with **Michael Stroll**. The timing and purpose of any work for Khashoggi remain unverified. [Senate BCCI report](https://irp.fas.org/congress/1992_rpt/bcci/11intel.htm) · [Walsh report](https://irp.fas.org/offdocs/walsh/chap_31.htm) · [Ward’s reporting as quoted by Law & Crime](https://lawandcrime.com/high-profile/investigative-journalist-explains-why-jeffrey-epstein-might-have-needed-a-fake-passport/) · [Stroll v. Epstein](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/district-courts/FSupp/818/640/1491208/) |
| **Starr and Lefkowitz → Epstein’s defense** | Starr served **William French Smith** from 1981 to 1983, before Meese became attorney general. Reagan nominated Starr to the D.C. Circuit in 1983. Lefkowitz served in **both Bush administrations**, with his first documented White House role in 1991. On **September 24, 2007**, Lefkowitz asked a federal prosecutor to keep Epstein’s agreement from becoming public. Later that year, Starr sought DOJ review of the provision dealing with monetary damages for victims. DOJ identifies **Alexander Acosta** as the U.S. attorney who approved the agreement. [Starr’s congressional biography](https://www.congress.gov/105/chrg/CHRG-105hhrg53367/CHRG-105hhrg53367.pdf) · [Lefkowitz oral history](https://millercenter.org/the-presidency/presidential-oral-histories/jay-lefkowitz-oral-history) · [Doe v. United States](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/district-courts/florida/flsdce/9:2008cv80736/317867/435/) · [DOJ OPR report](https://www.epstein-search.com/document/263/pdf) · [DOJ executive summary](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/11/12/epstein._executive_summary.pdf) |
| **George H.W. Bush → the archive** | The Bush library identifies a **letter from Khashoggi to Vice President Bush** about a *Washington Times* article. The FOIA finding aid covers numerous names and institutions. A released **August 2019 FBI email chain** records an allegation mentioning Bush. I found no corroboration for that allegation or a record establishing a direct Bush–Epstein relationship. [Bush Presidential Library finding aid](https://www.bush41library.gov/digital-research-room/finding-aid/foia/records-jeffrey-epstein-ghislaine-maxwell-etc) · [Released email, EFTA00147661](https://epstein-data.com/EFTA00147661) · [Reporting on the released record](https://www.skeptic.org.uk/2026/02/what-the-epstein-files-tell-us-about-conspiracy-theories-and-about-skeptics/) |
